<role>
You are a narrow residual discovery reader. Your complete job is to find only material remainders that survive accounting for the current position's adopted decision machinery. Do not inventory everything pending. Do not give advice, select a graph, activate pressure, or score quality.
</role>

<authority>
The complete source is authoritative. Prior interpretations are fallible context, not source truth. Preserve speaker ownership and modal force. Source-supported inference is allowed; outside facts are forbidden. Omitted implementation detail is not affirmative evidence of absence.
</authority>

<residual_operation>
1. Account for what the current position already assigns, governs, safeguards, conditions, schedules, or deliberately defers for the present decision horizon.
2. Subtract that decision machinery and the pending work it already governs.
3. Emit only the materially distinct remainder affirmatively supported by the source.

RESIDUAL DECISION GAP: a materially distinct question, dependency, ownership gap, or tension that remains outside the adopted machinery after subtraction.

RESIDUAL RECONSIDERATION DEPENDENCY: materially distinct later evidence, an event, or a dependency failure outside the adopted machinery that would require reconsidering an otherwise current position.

Pending does not equal residual. Deferred does not equal unowned. A scheduled decision may leave its final outcome unselected while operationalizing the decision work. An existing threshold, benchmark, pause rule, fallback, exit, or scheduled review is not itself newly recovered pressure.
</residual_operation>

<evidence>
For every supported residual, cite exact source aliases that collectively establish both the material dependency or question and why the current position's adopted machinery does not fully handle it. Preserve the evidence for source-first review; do not rank evidence strength.
</evidence>

<examples>
- One-time installation funding plus unassigned recurring staffing and operating ownership can leave a residual decision gap.
- A supplier redesign governed by parallel proposals, milestones, fallback, criteria, and a fixed decision remains pending but is not residual merely because the final design is unselected.
- Independent evidence that defeats a premise of an otherwise current decision can be a residual reconsideration dependency when no adopted mechanism already governs that failure.
- A missing detail supports ambiguity only when a material residual is plausible and the source cannot establish whether it remains outside the adopted machinery.
</examples>

<output_rules>
Return no_supported_record_observed with an empty array when no distinct residual remains. Return ambiguous_review only for one or more ambiguous records and no supported record. Return records_present only for at least one supported residual. Cite exact source aliases and return schema-valid JSON only.
</output_rules>

<authoritative_source>
{"aliases":[{"alias":"e001","speaker":"user","text":"I run a small contemporary dance company preparing a six-city relaxed-performance tour. The venues are signed, the work is rehearsed, and an arts grant paid for captions, tactile maps, and quiet-room kits. What still worries me is the human coordination around patrons who need different arrangements in different cities. Everyone agrees access matters, but agreement is not the same as somebody owning the work every week.","text_sha256":"8ed213cf95b530cd198d6b884d00855212bc09eee19dafc5d891037a6dc51adf","turn_index":1},{"alias":"e002","speaker":"assistant","text":"Map the current tour commitments first, then ask each plausible owner what they have actually accepted. Separate technical delivery, venue-night duties, travel booking, and ongoing coordination; they may sound adjacent while belonging to different people.","text_sha256":"1d2567ee9b78d609d5dd81681c026183e9165f1a065e99dbc84563e4fc1a9c70","turn_index":1},{"alias":"e003","speaker":"user","text":"The artistic director owns rehearsals and the relaxed-performance script. Each venue owns evacuation, front-of-house staffing, and the quiet room during its performance. BrightLine supplies caption hardware and an operator. Our tour manager books company travel and freight. The board approved all six dates and a 162,000-euro tour budget. The first performance is seven weeks away.","text_sha256":"a27b7cd62bddd408e0d70b8badf15048b3afde621704eb05fa6202c05560a8af","turn_index":2},{"alias":"e004","speaker":"assistant","text":"Who currently receives patron access requests, reconciles them across venues, follows up before travel, and checks that the promised arrangement survived a schedule change? Those are recurring tasks rather than equipment purchases.","text_sha256":"62489e657f5734737202f65309394bab3612635d300a2c103667d604129d1762","turn_index":2},{"alias":"e005","speaker":"user","text":"At the moment requests arrive through six venue forms, our general inbox, and sometimes the box-office phone. During the pilot night, I personally copied them into a spreadsheet and called three patrons. That took eleven hours in one week. For the tour we expect between twenty-five and forty requests per city, including seating, low-light entry, caption sightlines, companion tickets, and quiet arrival times.","text_sha256":"c96851710952b520f9a7722b934a21eb2db40be8b70aa87ae5b808d4750418a6","turn_index":3},{"alias":"e006","speaker":"assistant","text":"Ask the venues whether their responsibility extends beyond their own building and date. Also ask whether the tour manager or caption contractor has accepted communication and follow-through rather than assuming it fits their titles.","text_sha256":"f1954a795fdee271981707e2b023953c620cd28dbbc4d85068cc5e2bffa548a6","turn_index":3},{"alias":"e007","speaker":"user","text":"The venue contracts are explicit: each access manager handles requests from five days before its own performance until doors close. They do not consolidate earlier messages or coordinate a patron attending in more than one city. Four access managers wrote that their hours cannot begin earlier without a fee amendment. The two municipal venues cannot accept work outside their building under union rules.","text_sha256":"869fa791cf1050146651200e6a93164377289b5384aa908071372faaf2798f50","turn_index":4},{"alias":"e008","speaker":"assistant","text":"What did your internal team and BrightLine say? Preserve their exact scope and any capacity limits.","text_sha256":"38f4deb7db9ffb8eedaf29ec1312f68dd8d8eb16277b11eea2dfcc21890f510c","turn_index":4},{"alias":"e009","speaker":"user","text":"The tour manager said her signed role covers company travel, accommodation, freight, and daily schedules. She will forward a patron message but will not manage medical or access information, and her workload is already full. BrightLine's contract covers caption files, hardware, and the operator; it excludes ticketing, patron communication, transport, and venue coordination. The artistic director said the rehearsal team cannot hold personal access details.","text_sha256":"b3f1938c9f42e79be34fce1e34572334485d5a46ec7f75f291955d4b9f786ea9","turn_index":5},{"alias":"e010","speaker":"assistant","text":"That narrows the plausible internal owners. Is there a partner organization that can take the recurring work, or only advise on how it should be done?","text_sha256":"67ae9c1ad1899da81edb8fa79e27ae0c68bfed005af6c23df3f96599664a3f86","turn_index":5},{"alias":"e011","speaker":"user","text":"Open Door Arts helped design the pilot. Its director confirmed they can review forms, train staff for two half-days, and join one post-tour debrief. Their charity insurance does not cover operating another company's bookings, holding patron contact details, or being on call during the tour. They declined the coordinator role in writing but offered a checklist and training within the existing partnership fee.","text_sha256":"7b3e1c33235a4b64a98bfe92e3c42c69a82e3eae024b238c80f9068fb853ddb1","turn_index":6},{"alias":"e012","speaker":"assistant","text":"What funding was approved for staff time, as distinct from access materials and advice? A broad grant label can hide a narrow budget restriction.","text_sha256":"62c96393a598199583c67b066761aedd80ab25dc547fdc0d9c0dd20501dab723","turn_index":6},{"alias":"e013","speaker":"user","text":"The grant schedule pays 18,000 euros for caption equipment and operation, 7,500 for tactile maps and quiet-room kits, and 3,000 for Open Door's training. It prohibits moving those lines into salaries without prior approval. The company's general tour contingency is 6,000 euros, but the board reserved it for venue closure, freight, or performer illness. There is no staff line for cross-city patron coordination.","text_sha256":"f0d92e993368d7ccde3a5e03f74a9fb64ed843473225592c5ceb50d5366c965a","turn_index":7},{"alias":"e014","speaker":"assistant","text":"Has the board considered assigning and funding that work from another line, or did it only acknowledge the issue?","text_sha256":"479eb601ed767d1feab3acebebb494d74a9a34a51af6f61a7dc4751dc6130100","turn_index":7},{"alias":"e015","speaker":"user","text":"The board minutes from Monday acknowledge an estimated twelve to sixteen hours per city. The artistic director, tour manager, producer, and venue representatives each confirmed their narrower duties. The board voted to keep the signed dates and existing budget but did not assign the recurring work or approve a salary amendment. It asked me to return with options, even though I am already the executive producer and cannot personally cover six cities.","text_sha256":"8c797c595d19d975fb127d22d774c8d2a37e061049cfa8d7237ef35193d87247","turn_index":8},{"alias":"e016","speaker":"assistant","text":"Check whether any adopted operating procedure closes part of the problem. Incident response, data handling, and same-night assistance may already be owned even if the cross-city work is not.","text_sha256":"4b124ecb02582331ce12fc8655668feb72282f6b095ebddf55a22837ebd3857a","turn_index":8},{"alias":"e017","speaker":"user","text":"Yes. The stage manager owns incidents involving performers and patrons once the company arrives at a venue. Venue access managers own same-night adjustments. Our data policy lets a designated company employee hold access requests in the encrypted ticketing account and requires deletion thirty days after the tour. The tour manager can book an accessible hotel room once somebody provides the requirement. None of those procedures names who gathers, reconciles, confirms, and hands off the requests before each venue's five-day window.","text_sha256":"4d1e9b86460fd051bc7989629adbc98f158f4cc03d5d8546d313183637f26f19","turn_index":9},{"alias":"e018","speaker":"assistant","text":"That distinction should stay concrete. Have you tested whether the work can be divided among existing roles without creating gaps at the handoffs?","text_sha256":"d21d70c43e9817faab42f1fc846458ec76a03776bb2befa5828ad62ef041d138","turn_index":9},{"alias":"e019","speaker":"user","text":"We tested that during the pilot. The box office answered ticket questions, BrightLine checked caption seats, and the venue handled arrival. Nobody noticed that a patron's companion ticket had been changed when the caption block moved. I caught it because the patron emailed me directly. The pilot report recommends one named person from first request through venue handoff; splitting the spreadsheet by department recreated the same missed confirmation twice.","text_sha256":"4bd6e72982b2c99d50bf5683c2331c8f5b4b699f826953b4777daf75b64b8323","turn_index":10},{"alias":"e020","speaker":"assistant","text":"Are there credible ways to cover it before the first date, and do any of them already have authority or money?","text_sha256":"0de872c566b074ec05f857498fcb350bab0db511ee28d7cea1bb78e867182007","turn_index":10},{"alias":"e021","speaker":"user","text":"I have three options: hire a part-time coordinator for ten weeks, pay Open Door to subcontract someone if its insurer approves, or reduce the tour to venues willing to start their access hours earlier. None is adopted. The treasurer says a salary needs either new unrestricted funding or a board transfer from contingency. Open Door has not offered a subcontract, and changing venues would breach signed dates.","text_sha256":"6673e6b240548f0e8e13449d76894e185a556c26910b1bcd7a1e38689ea2a1fb","turn_index":11},{"alias":"e022","speaker":"assistant","text":"How does the possible grant next spring relate to these six signed dates? Does the board treat it as financing this tour or only later work?","text_sha256":"e53542fa0f6ddeeb9040a793936cca324d5c094a40da88778c08b52b956b17aa","turn_index":11},{"alias":"e023","speaker":"user","text":"No. We may apply next spring for a larger access grant, but it would fund a later tour and has no bearing on these six signed dates. The board confirmed this tour proceeds under the current agreements. For these dates it kept Friday's staffing options on its own agenda; it is not waiting for a future award, venue renewal, or external approval before acting.","text_sha256":"0b45c448bbcb06378d3dcb73b1d0d837e98b6234b20696ca6067c3e2719b9a96","turn_index":12},{"alias":"e024","speaker":"assistant","text":"What evidence remains to gather for the board's near-term options, and who owns that preparation?","text_sha256":"a21601c23df444dcedfb3205f4fdd6fe6c3416b9ea27fee655df5bba756cb5b6","turn_index":12},{"alias":"e025","speaker":"user","text":"The treasurer will price a ten-week contract, Open Door will answer the insurance question, and the producer will calculate amendment costs from the six venues. Those figures are due Friday. Rehearsals, venue calls, caption-file delivery, and the quiet-room kit shipment continue on their signed schedules.","text_sha256":"6096309d186f994868feb51e72c8e943bf095bc2084a8dda229518d062df184f","turn_index":13},{"alias":"e026","speaker":"assistant","text":"Before the board meets, verify that the material budget has not been mistaken for staff funding and that the options paper preserves the existing role boundaries.","text_sha256":"6c97a459dcb4088ae0fba7f8dea2271a258465af0b6258bf7300287b37b82858","turn_index":13},{"alias":"e027","speaker":"user","text":"I checked. The 7,500-euro line is restricted to maps, signage, lamps, cushions, and shipping; it cannot pay wages. The options paper now quotes the venue, tour-manager, BrightLine, and Open Door limits rather than assuming their job titles cover more. I have not recommended one option yet because the three cost replies are still due.","text_sha256":"2f26005d407860557c1ba1cc72ec50fd69ae105959c0c53bc6f84b58cadd738d","turn_index":14},{"alias":"e028","speaker":"assistant","text":"I can help format the options paper around cost, authority, handoffs, and timing while leaving the board to choose how it will cover the work.","text_sha256":"7e74ed5c3b1bfec84bc48432ee82813971292118cd1817a3ceaa4d7d694aaa09","turn_index":14}],"message_count":28,"path":"research/lolla-r4-separated-surface-experiment-v1-source-freeze-2026-07-14/sources/r4s1-case03-relaxed-performance-tour.json","sha256":"f3485f9e59f9470bb4927a7c13d9c799c17145e8939d1c0b8b093535281f9549"}
</authoritative_source>

<task>
Perform residual accounting and subtraction over the complete source. Return exactly one review for residual_decision_gap and one for residual_reconsideration_dependency, in either order, with at most two records per review. Preserve exact aliases, speaker ownership, and modal force. Do not give advice, select a graph, or score quality.
</task>

global_limitations.description: Limits applying to the whole read; empty if none.

reviews.description: Exactly one review for each residual surface.

outcome.description: Present, quiet, or ambiguous result of this residual review.

records.description: Zero to two candidates for this residual surface.

evidence_ids.description: Exact source aliases that collectively establish the material dependency or question and why adopted machinery does not fully handle it.

interpretation.description: Concise meaning of this residual without advice.

limitations.description: Residual uncertainty or scope limit; use an empty string if none.

support.description: Whether the source supports the residual or leaves it ambiguous.
